buoyant_surface.source: closed gull-wing envelope rebuilt from the package station table (same loft as its build_model.py); NOT a measured hull - no offsets exist. At the package's drawn waterline (z=0) it displaces ~4.9 m3, far more than the 2.1-3.0 t references: the proxy hull form and/or its waterline datum are not consistent.

placement_in_exo_frame.source: modelling_assumption: boat stern 0.1 m forward of the EXO rear deck plate edge (x = 2.2 m), centred between the float rows; stern/aft cabin under the frame bays, bow 5.15 m beyond the end frame. Vertical position and attitude come from the boat's own flotation, never from this transform.

line_presets.title: Aft breasts + backward springs (v0.3 default)
line_presets.note: EXO aft posts -> stern cleats, EXO forward posts -> midship cleats aft of them: balanced at rest, the springs can carry a forward push

line_presets.title: Four lines all running forward (anatomy figure, 28/10)
line_presets.note: EXO x 2.18 and 4.87 -> boat cleats forward of each (stern x 0.30, midship x 4.30): holds the boat against a tow or braking only; cannot transmit a forward push from the pods (all lines go slack)

line_presets.title: Long push springs + forward breasts
line_presets.note: EXO forward posts -> stern cleats (long, mostly longitudinal: carry the pods' push efficiently) and EXO aft posts -> midship cleats forward (carry a tow/brake and restrain yaw)

line_presets.title: Six lines: breasts + push springs + tow springs
line_presets.note: breasts at the stern cleats from the aft posts, long push springs from the forward posts to the stern cleats, tow springs from the aft posts to the midship cleats

line_presets.title: Two stern fenders (push bars) + tow lines to the midship cleats
line_presets.note: two compression-only fenders between the EXO rear deck edge (x 2.1) and the boat's transom at the quarters carry the pods' push directly (pusher-tug arrangement); the two lines from the aft posts to the midship cleats carry a tow and hold the boat against the fenders; yaw is restrained by the fender pair in compression and the lines in tension

line_presets.title: Two stern fenders + crossed stern lines + tow lines
line_presets.note: fenders as above; crossed lines from the aft posts to the opposite stern cleats (face wires) restrain yaw and sway; tow lines to the midship cleats for the tow case

line_presets.title: Two stern fenders + the best line diagonals
line_presets.note: fenders as above plus the arrangement the line sweep ranks first (aft posts -> midship cleats, forward posts -> stern cleats)

line_presets.title: Rigid coupling: four bilateral struts (k = 1 MN/m)
line_presets.note: limit case of a bolted/rigid connection between the EXO frame and the boat: struts at the aft posts -> stern cleats and forward posts -> midship cleats, bilateral and very stiff; the element loads are what a rigid coupling must carry

host_boat.lines_note: assumed arrangement: two aft breast lines (EXO aft posts -> stern cleats, pulling the boat slightly aft) and two springs (EXO forward posts -> midship cleats aft of them, pulling the boat forward) so that the horizontal line forces can balance; attachment points are not measured

line_defaults.source: modelling_assumption: 'slightly tense' lines = linear springs about a small pretension. A bare taut 10-12 mm polyester line of 1-2 m is ~5-10x stiffer and goes slack in compression (nonlinear, not modelled); the response flags when the dynamic tension amplitude exceeds the pretension.

notes: The boat and the EXO are two separate floating bodies; each has its own still-water equilibrium.

Still water: coupled equilibrium of both bodies with tension-only line springs (L0 = L_nominal - T0/k): the boat shifts/yaws from the nominal berth until the line forces balance; equilibrium tensions (possibly slack) feed the wave model.
Wave response: both bodies in one Capytaine problem (hydrodynamic interaction included), 12 DOF, lines as linear springs.

thrust_model.note: thrust = fraction x bollard thrust, independent of speed (optimistic at speed: a rim drive's thrust falls with advance speed)

exo.note: per float row: ITTC-57 friction on the wetted area x (1+k) + Cd x submerged frontal area of one float for the nose/flat-end junctions and gaps (ASSUMED coefficients; the flat-to-flat junction of the rear and middle floats and the nose-to-flat junction of the middle and end floats are not resolved)

boat.note: ITTC-57 friction on the proxy hull's wetted area x (1+k) x appendages (keel, rudder, propeller) + residuary C_R = c (Fr/0.2)^n on the wetted area (ASSUMED; the proxy hull is not the real hull)

resistance.drag_points: EXO: resultant at the centroid of the submerged float volume (world); boat: at its centre of buoyancy

propulsion.label: QUASI-STATIC: steady state, thrust = total resistance, no wave-added resistance, wind or current; line loads are what the arrangement must carry to push/tow the other body

visual_overrides.reason: User corrections 2026-10-28: (1) the two longitudinal walkway plates drawn in the middle and end bays do not exist; (2) the two transverse base members crossing the gap between the float rows at deck level (x = 3.5 m and 4.95 m) do not exist either - they are the only members that intersect the berthed Hydronaute; (3) 18:21: the top side rails of the end (panel) bay do not exist. Names may be qualified by section (SECTION/name) when the same name occurs in several sections. The space between the float rows is open so the boat can be berthed inside the frame.

visual_overrides.buoyancy_effect: none - only the six floats are buoyant surfaces
